title: Elastic Threshold Attention: Learned Contextual Sparsity for Long-Context Decoding
summary: ETA replaces fixed-heuristic sparse attention (and dense FlashAttention decoding) with per-query learned thresholds that hard-prune KV blocks, trained via multiplicative suppression of sub-threshold logits rather than token deletion. The cost is substantial: the policy must be learned during pretraining, inference requires a custom Triton decode kernel, and deployment-quality thresholds need offline per-domain calibration to remove predictor overhead. It can fail on workloads unlike the training distribution, where predicted thresholds may prune context needed for retrieval or reasoning, and the reported quality parity is demonstrated only at 1.45B scale, so transfer to larger or API-served models is unverified.
rationale: The reader cannot pretrain models and relies on existing checkpoints or APIs, so an architecture that must be trained from scratch is not adoptable now, but the calibration-and-kernel pattern is worth tracking as sparse long-context serving matures.

claims.statement: ETA replaces fixed-heuristic sparse attention (and dense FlashAttention decoding) with per-query learned thresholds that hard-prune KV blocks, trained via multiplicative suppression of sub-threshold logits rather than token deletion. The cost is substantial: the policy must be learned during pretraining, inference requires a custom Triton decode kernel, and deployment-quality thresholds need offline per-domain calibration to remove predictor overhead. It can fail on workloads unlike the training distribution, where predicted thresholds may prune context needed for retrieval or reasoning, and the reported quality parity is demonstrated only at 1.45B scale, so transfer to larger or API-served models is unverified.
Up to 2.5x wall-clock decode speedup over FlashAttention-2 on sequences up to 512K tokens, at ~38% active decode density with quality matching dense attention on a 1.45B pretrained model.
